text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Leader of legal Islamist party Nahda says party is not a religious one and so he has no fears of seeing it banned under the proposed new constitution.
- Maghreb-Europe gas pipeline will go on stream on Nov 9.
- Transport minister inaugurates Hassi R'mel airport Nov 9.
- Main workers' Union Generale des Travailleurs Algeriens will field its own candidates in parliamentary elections planned for the first half of 1997.
- State-owned advertising company, Agence Nationale d'Edition et de Publicite, prints 400,000 posters for the constitution referendum campaign.
- Socialist Forces Front dissidents, known as Tizi-Ouzou Group, intend to set up their own party.
